The Third Conditional - Talking Hypothetically About the Past
When talking about unreal situations in the past, the third conditional is used.

The third conditional is used to talk about past regrets. You can use would have, should have and could have to discuss hypothetical situations in the past.
Could have is used to represent that a past action was possible and that the user could have done something, but didn't.
Example: We could have heard Prince play!

Should have is used to represent regret about something that was done or not done in the past.
Example: We should have studied harder for the exam!
Should have can also be used to offer someone advice.
Example: You should have studied harder for the exam!

Would have is used in the past to represent something that didn't occur.
Example: Maybe if you had lived in another era you would have been a lot happier.

You use wish, plus the past form of the verb or the past participle of the verb to talk about imaginary situations in the past, present or future.

Wishes and sentences in the second and third conditional infer that what you want or wanted is probably not possible, or for some reason impossible and that you regret what happened in the past.

You use wish + Simple Past to talk about wishes in the present or future.

For example:
Sometimes I wish I lived in a different country.
(I don't live in a different country.)

You use wish + had + past participle to talk about wishes about past situations.

For example:
I wish I had had my umbrella!
(I didn't have my umbrella.)

images.text:
Sally: Do you ever wonder what it would have been like if you had been born in a different era?
Vanessa: If I had been born in another time period I wouldn't have come to America.
Sally: Why not?
Vanessa: There wouldn't have been the means of communication or transportation that there is now. I think those things make it easier for people to move around because you can easily and immediately travel or communicate with people overseas. They made it easier for me.
Sally: True. Sometimes I wish I lived in a different country. I wish I spoke another language.

Vanessa: You still can. Hey, Peter!
Peter: What's up? It's awful outside!
Vanessa: What's bugging you? You look grumpy.

Peter: Can't you see I'm drenched? I wish I had had my umbrella! The weatherman should have said rain, if he had known! Can't trust those guys!
Sally: Hey Pete! If you had had the choice when would you have chosen to be born?
Peter: That's a ludicrous question. I can't even fathom being born at another point in time.
Vanessa: Don't be such a stick in the mud. Maybe if you had lived in another era you would have been a lot happier.

Sally: Sometimes I wish we could go back to the Jazz Era in New Orleans.
Vanessa: Ohh that does sound rather intriguing! If I had been given a choice, I would have also picked that time and place. Imagine we would have worn all those lovely drop-waist dresses.
Peter: As much as this is a stupid conversation, that is a super cool idea!
Sally: That's it Peter. Let your imagination blossom!
